_note: Documentation only: no code reads this file at runtime. It records the public figures behind Nas, with the status of each, for the team and for the assumptions table. Status: ANCHORED = the team opened the source URL and checked the figure (MoDEE figures on 2026-10-09; 'retrieved' where recorded); TEAM_CONFIRMED = confirmed by the team, no source link recorded yet; CITED_UNVERIFIED = quoted by our AI-assisted desk research (Qwen, 'Amman in a Box') with a source we could not open or confirm (VALIDATION.md and seed_census.py call these CITED). The 33 engine constants in sim/assumptions.py (26 for ID renewal and shared travel, 7 for everyday_travel) are all ASSUMPTION; entries here only give context for them. The fuel entries (fuel_prices_oct_2026, naf_fuel_support_jd_month) give context for the everyday_travel presets; the health_insurance_* and jpfhs_* entries are for a planned third sector (Royal Court medical exemption) and are not used yet. Entries whose id starts with research_doc_ are figures from the team's research doc that must NOT be reused (see their notes). Never present a CITED_UNVERIFIED figure as an official statistic. Last checked 2026-10-10.

internet_use_individuals_jordan.source_name: MoDEE 2024 Household ICT Usage and Access Survey (results announcement)
internet_use_individuals_jordan.quote: The proportion of individuals who used the internet increased from 92.5% in 2023 to 95.6% in 2024.
internet_use_individuals_jordan.notes: National, all ages; no age breakdown on the page. seed_census.py uses it as the share of synthetic adults with a smartphone and hits it exactly (95.6%, 956 of 1,000). The age gradient (older people more often without one) is an ASSUMPTION.

smartphone_households_amman.source_name: MoDEE 2024 Household ICT Usage and Access Survey (results announcement)
smartphone_households_amman.notes: Household-level: a household having a smartphone does not mean every elderly member can use one. That is exactly the 'offline with a helper' case in the engine.

egov_use_individuals_jordan.source_name: MoDEE 2024 Household ICT Usage and Access Survey (results announcement)
egov_use_individuals_jordan.quote: 38.1% of individuals had accessed at least one e-government service
egov_use_individuals_jordan.notes: Context for the pitch: connectivity is near-universal, e-service use is not.

id_renewal_fee_jd.source_name: Confirmed by the team; add the CSPD link here if one is found
id_renewal_fee_jd.notes: JD 2 is the ID renewal fee, used as fee_jd in every scenario. The JD 1 the desk research cited (cspd.gov.jo e-services page) is for a different service: issuing a previously registered document electronically.

share_female.source_name: DoS figures as reported by The Jordan Times (Facebook post)
share_female.notes: Includes non-Jordanians (male-skewed migrant workforce). seed_census.py uses 53% male / 47% female, i.e. this figure as quoted by the research (tagged CITED there), for both its datasets.

disability_65_plus.source_name: UNFPA Arab States, Jordan country profile
disability_65_plus.notes: Any functional difficulty, all domains (seeing, hearing, walking...). Our seed models only mobility (limited/wheelchair), so this is an upper bound, not a direct input. PDF too large to verify automatically.

disability_overall_5_plus.source_name: 2015 Census (Washington Group) as cited by Humanity & Inclusion briefing paper 2023
disability_overall_5_plus.notes: All domains. Walking difficulty alone was reported at ~7% (secondary source).

female_labour_force_participation.notes: World Bank API was down (502) when we tried to confirm. Seed 'works' rates are employment, not participation.

bus_fare_jd_range.source_name: Transportation Research Interdisciplinary Perspectives article; BRT fare from expat guides
bus_fare_jd_range.notes: Context for BUS_FARE_JD only. Publisher blocked automated access (403). Our frozen BUS_FARE_JD 0.45 is an ASSUMPTION set before any scenario ran; it happens to lie inside this range.

bus_wait_peak_minutes.source_name: The Open Transportation Journal, vol 13, p 227
bus_wait_peak_minutes.notes: Context for BUS_FIRST_WAIT_MIN and BUS_WAIT_PLUS_TRANSFER_MIN only. A peak-hour wait; our frozen values (10 min first wait + 15 min per transfer) are ASSUMPTIONS, set for off-peak visits. BUS_WAIT_PLUS_TRANSFER_MIN is in the ±20% robustness check. A known gap, stated honestly.

district_population_2015.source_name: 2015 Census via GAM, as tabulated on Wikipedia 'Amman'
district_population_2015.notes: Seven of the 22 districts shown here; seed_census.py holds all 22 rows as quoted by the research and draws every citizen's district from their relative shares (VALIDATION.md, district table). Each district then maps to one of our 8 engine areas. Not yet checked against a GAM/DoS table, hence CITED_UNVERIFIED.

cspd_offices_amman.notes: The baseline scenario IS this network: the 7 offices are in sites.json (real: true) with their addresses from this page, located once with OpenStreetMap Nominatim (precision recorded per site). The 8 other sites are generic snap sites, one per engine area.

cspd_office_hours.source_name: CSPD's published office hours (cspd.gov.jo), read by the team on 2026-10-09
cspd_office_hours.notes: Used as the baseline hours of all 7 offices. The exact page URL was not recorded, so this stays TEAM_CONFIRMED; add the URL here (and 'retrieved') to make it ANCHORED. A Fri/Sat 10:00-14:00 line on CSPD's site is not modelled: it may be contact-centre hours.

fuel_prices_oct_2026.scope: Jordan national, retail fuel prices for October 2026
fuel_prices_oct_2026.source_name: Fuel Pricing Committee decision for October 2026, as reported by Jordan News (2026-10-01)
fuel_prices_oct_2026.notes: CITED: a press report of the committee's decision, read by the team on 2026-10-10; the committee's own statement was not opened. Context for the everyday_travel sector: the fuel_plus_5 preset is this rise (+0.05 JD/L on 90-octane, about +5%), and the frontend shows '90-octane 1.050 JD/L' next to the fuel stepper (config.js FUEL_PRICE_90_JD, display only). The engine works in % changes, not JD/L, so no engine constant comes from this figure. The fuel_plus_25_fares preset is modelled on the 2012 subsidy removal (fuel and fares raised together); 2012 is referenced as context only, no 2012 figure is anchored.

naf_fuel_support_jd_month.scope: National Aid Fund beneficiary families, JD per month
naf_fuel_support_jd_month.source_name: Ammon News report on the National Aid Fund's fuel support
naf_fuel_support_jd_month.notes: CITED (press report): 8-14 JD a month per beneficiary family. Context for the cash_support lever only: the fuel_plus_25_support preset gives 14 JD/month to the low_income group, and the travel fix grid tries 8 / 14 / 20 JD. Our cash support is per synthetic resident, not per family, and low_income is the bottom 30% of synthetic income, not the NAF caseload.

health_insurance_jordan_2015.scope: Jordan national, all ages (2015 General Population and Housing Census)
health_insurance_jordan_2015.source_name: Department of Statistics, 'Health Insurance in Jordan: analytical paper prepared according to the results of the General Population and Housing Census 2015'
health_insurance_jordan_2015.notes: Opened by the team on 2026-10-10 (the official DoS PDF). For the planned 'Royal Court medical exemption' sector; nothing reads it yet. The ~56% total-population figure is the paper's rounded national rate. All children under 6 are insured by the Ministry of Health, so all-ages rates understate adult uninsurance. The lowest-covered age group is 15-34. The paper also says 38% of the INSURED non-Jordanians are under special arrangements: that is not an insurance rate (see research_doc_non_jordanians_insured_38).

health_insurance_amman_2015.source_name: Department of Statistics, 'Health Insurance in Jordan' (Census 2015 analytical paper)
health_insurance_amman_2015.recommended_for_engine: Amman Jordanians aged 16+ uninsured: about 45-50%. The ANCHORED figure is 44.8% (all ages); it includes children under 6, who are all insured, so adults are higher. The 45-50% adult range is our ASSUMPTION built on that anchor, not a published figure.
health_insurance_amman_2015.notes: Amman and Zarqa are the lowest-covered governorates (about 41% of their total population insured). Our synthetic population is Jordanian nationals 16+, so the Jordanians figure (55.2% insured / 44.8% not) is the relevant one, not the 41.2% total-population figure (which mixes in non-Jordanians at 16.4-16.8% insured). Say '2015 census' on stage: it is a 2015 figure, not today's.

jpfhs_2023_health_insurance.scope: Jordan national; ever-married women 15-49 and men 15-49
jpfhs_2023_health_insurance.source_name: Jordan Population and Family Health Survey 2023, summary report (DoS / DHS Program)
jpfhs_2023_health_insurance.notes: A more recent national cross-check of the 2015 census rates, for adults of working age. No Amman breakdown is used from it.

research_doc_jordanians_insured_76_8.scope: Jordanians, national (as quoted in the team's research doc on the Amman uninsured rate)
research_doc_jordanians_insured_76_8.source_name: BMC Health Services Research article (2024), PMC11378627, as quoted in the team's research doc
research_doc_jordanians_insured_76_8.notes: DO NOT USE. The breakdown the article gives does not add up (65.6 + 6.8 + 12.5 = 84.9, not 76.8), the figure carries no year, and the article itself cites the DoS 2015 paper for most of its numbers. Use health_insurance_jordan_2015 (68.7% of Jordanians insured) and health_insurance_amman_2015 instead.

research_doc_non_jordanians_insured_38.scope: Non-Jordanians (as quoted in the team's research doc)
research_doc_non_jordanians_insured_38.source_name: Team research doc, misreading the DoS 2015 Health Insurance paper
research_doc_non_jordanians_insured_38.notes: DO NOT USE. The research doc's '38% of non-Jordanians insured' conflates two different DoS statements: 25.3% of non-Jordanians are insured (16.4-16.8% in Amman), and 38% of the INSURED non-Jordanians are covered under special arrangements.
